title: Data mart, data mesh and metadata-driven architectures

videos.script: A data mart is the warehouse cut down for one department: the sales team's tables, finance's tables. {{mart}} Built from the warehouse, a mart is a convenience. Built on its own, beside the warehouse, it is a second answer to the same question. {{independent}} Ana asks three marts for December's revenue and gets three numbers. Each one is defensible. None of them agrees with the others. {{three}} The cure is old: one list of business processes, one set of shared dimensions, and a name for every measure. Kimball called it the bus matrix. {{bus}} Data mesh asks the next question. In a company with fifty teams, who owns all this? Its answer: the teams that produce the data own it, and publish it as a product, with a contract. {{mesh}} A contract can be checked by a program. Ana writes one for the sales table, and watches it catch a renamed column. {{contract}} And when a warehouse has hundreds of tables, nobody should write each load by hand. The pipeline is generated from a list of sources. {{metadata}} None of these is free. The lesson ends with how to argue for one. {{argue}}
